intended_object: For a functor A : C ⥤ Grp D, with D cartesian monoidal, the group object in the functor category C ⥤ D that it induces: the underlying functor X ↦ (A X).X with unit, multiplication and inverse defined pointwise. This is the object part of the equivalence Grp(C ⥤ D) ≌ (C ⥤ Grp D). Inferred from the docstring, the module doc and the companion `functorObj`/`inverse`.
explanation:
The definition first builds the monoid object `M` in C ⥤ D. It does this by applying Mathlib's `monFunctorCategoryEquivalence` (its inverse direction) to A ⋙ Grp.forget₂Mon D. So the underlying functor, unit and multiplication are the pointwise ones from A.

It then adds an inverse natural transformation whose component at X is the inverse ι of the group object A.obj X. Naturality holds because each (A.map f) is a group-object morphism and therefore commutes with ι (`GrpObj.inv_hom`). The proofs of left_inv and right_inv work componentwise: lift and toUnit in the pointwise cartesian structure on C ⥤ D are computed objectwise, so the axioms reduce to the group axioms of each A.obj X. This is exactly the standard pointwise group object.

The generality is natural. C is an arbitrary category, and D only needs to be cartesian monoidal, which Mathlib's `GrpObj` requires anyway. Mathlib has the monoid version (`monFunctorCategoryEquivalence`) but no group-object counterpart of this equivalence. The library also checks the round trip with a `rfl` lemma, `inverseObj_pointwiseGrp`.
